answer: Require every new identity to solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle seeded by the current epoch, so each fake name costs real compute and electricity. Like layers of shale laid down one at a time, work cannot be faked in bulk or reused across epochs. A farm's identities pool in a shallow lagoon of cheap copies, but a prism of verification splits them apart: each puzzle solution is unique, time-bound, and publicly checkable, so clones either pay the full price per identity or stay dark.
